newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Danish coffee body to target younger market.
newsitem.headline: Danish coffee body to target younger market.

text.p: The Danish Coffee Roasters Association (DCRA) has launched an aggressive marketing drive aimed at persuading young people to develop a taste for coffee rather than soft drinks.

Jens Wang Jensen, a DCRA board member, told the Second International Coffee and Tea Symposium conference meeting in Vienna that if the younger generation was not targeted, the coffee industry would lose out badly to soft drinks firms.
"We started this campaign because we had the feeling that we were losing the younger generation," Jensen said after a presentation of the campaign on Wednesday afternoon.
Jensen said figures compiled in Denmark since 1989 showed how coffee consumption in the average household had declined to the advantage of soft drinks makers.
"Coffee consumption per household has gone down from 309 litres per household in 1994 to 290 litres in 1996.
"We are still the biggest, but these guys (soft drink producers) are coming," Jensen said.

He said that if the trend were to continue, the coffee industry would lose 15 percent or more of the Danish market, with consumption shrinking from a current level of 35,400 tonnes to 30,000 tonnes by 2008.
Denmark, Norway, Sweden and Finland are the biggest per capita coffee consumers in the world, with levels of 10 to 11 kg a year, compared with four kg per capita per year in the U.S.
Jensen said consumption figures from Norway, Germany and the Netherlands had shown a decline similar to that seen in Denmark.
As part of its new campaign, DCRA is using video advertising, posters and youth magazines to sell coffee to a new generation of consumers.
"What we are trying to explain to them is that there are many things you don't like the first time you try it, but you'll get used to it."
